subject.title: Regression: exec intermittently unavailable in isolated cron sessions (was fixed in 2026.4.1)

question: Should isolated cron runs fail only from structured pre-dispatch or tool-execution capability failures, or should certain model-authored unavailable-tool responses also change the recorded cron status?
rationale: The reporter’s current smoke does not reproduce the original wildcard path, while prior related reports show that heuristic post-run failure classification can mislabel successful work; maintainers need to choose the durable operator contract.

options.title: Use structured failure signals
options.body: Require tool-surface and execution layers to emit structured failures before cron status changes, avoiding text-based inference from the model response.

options.title: Add a warning outcome
options.body: Preserve `ok` only for completed turns but expose a distinct warning state for suspected model-reported capability loss.

options.title: Keep current status semantics
options.body: Leave status unchanged and rely on diagnostics until a reproducible routing or tool-construction failure is captured.

recommendation.title: Use structured failure signals
recommendation.body: Require tool-surface and execution layers to emit structured failures before cron status changes, avoiding text-based inference from the model response.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work covers the adjacent Codex runtime tool-surface contract and provides the strongest available history signal for this decision.
